fixtures.title: Descendant escape and causal work completeness
fixtures.prerequisites: a disposable native scope, direct launch plus one nested child, stable process identities, independent actor registration, and a declaration of which privileges and external services the worker may use.
fixtures.injected_fault: after W reaches first runnable instruction, D1 repeatedly creates D2 while C requests termination. Separate variants attempt explicit and silent Windows breakaway, a Linux migration out of the delegated subtree before kill, setsid or a new process group, nested Job/cgroup creation, and a synthetic external service creating work on request. The privileged migration variant runs only in a disposable privileged test target; it must not grant those privileges to a production worker. A denied attempt is an observed outcome, not a skipped variant.
fixtures.observation_oracle: E records every actor's requested creation, native identity, first execution and observed scope membership. C records effective permissions and actual result codes. The negative control deliberately permits an escape or external-service launch and must cause descendant_capture_complete to become false or unknown while scope_membership_complete may remain true. Killing a scope cannot make those two values equal by definition.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: close or fence admission, enumerate the exact managed scope, reconcile all registered actors and service receipts, and establish which actors terminated, survived or cannot be located. Preserve surviving out of scope actors as a contract failure when their capture was promised; clean them only through the separately approved harness cleanup identity.
fixtures.stop_condition: any actor running outside a promised captured boundary rejects that completeness claim. Any unrelated process affected triggers safety stop. Loss of actor or scope visibility yields unknown. Native mechanisms: S01, S05, S06, S32.

fixtures.title: Parent death before registration
fixtures.prerequisites: C independently observes native creation and durable registration barriers; W cannot perform external work before the admission gate is released.
fixtures.injected_fault: kill B separately before native creation; after creation begins but before it returns; after creation returns but before registration; during registration; after registration commits but before acknowledgment; and after acknowledgment but before normal supervision starts. For a proposed suspended creation sequence, add death before assignment and before resume. For creation-time membership, confirm W's first execution occurs within the scope even if B dies.
fixtures.observation_oracle: native creation result, stable process handle or pidfd, first instruction membership witness, registration commit witness and external acknowledgment must be separable. A missing response is not proof no child was created. The negative control intentionally opens the create-then-register gap and confirms that the oracle can see the orphan or unresolved launch.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: a new B epoch reconciles registered intent, actual scope contents and live process identities, then either adopts a still authorized execution or terminates it under the selected policy. It must not release two workers for one intent, launch a replacement before resolving the first launch, or report not_started solely because the registration record is absent.
fixtures.stop_condition: an unfenced worker performs work, two active executions are admitted, or the recovery policy loses a witnessed child: rejected. Unobservable creation/commit order: unknown. Failure to restore safe admission control: safety stop. Mechanisms: S02, S03, S06, S07.

fixtures.title: Last handle and scope lifetime
fixtures.prerequisites: explicit ownership inventory for Job handles, pidfds, inherited descriptors and any monitor references; a test process deliberately retains one extra reference.
fixtures.injected_fault: crash B while another actor retains a duplicated or inherited Job handle. Compare with a variant in which B holds the last Job handle under kill-on-close. On Linux, kill the manager without explicitly killing the cgroup, then compare with the selected supervisor cleanup path. Hold a terminal descriptor open after W exits in another variant.
fixtures.observation_oracle: E captures reference ownership transfers, native member state and termination events. Broker death must not be inferred to mean last-handle closure or cgroup destruction. The intentionally retained reference must remain visible to the oracle and prevent premature settled status.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: determine whether the scope survived, whether its identity can be reattached safely, and whether cleanup killed only owned members. Releasing observer references happens after the evidence window so the observer itself does not cause an apparent successful kill-on-close result.
fixtures.stop_condition: settlement while a required actor survives rejects; inability to distinguish which handle kept the scope alive yields unknown. Harness cleanup causing an effect before it was observed invalidates that cell. Mechanisms: S01, S32, S05, S37.

fixtures.title: Undrained terminal teardown
fixtures.prerequisites: W writes numbered output records faster than the consumer drains; C confirms actual backpressure rather than assuming a pipe capacity. An independent watchdog and independent exit observer remain responsive.
fixtures.injected_fault: stop the output consumer at output_blocked, then close the terminal host or invoke the native terminal teardown. Run separate policies that continue draining, deliberately truncate by closing output, and crash the terminal client. Run distinct Windows pre26100 and 26100-or-later profiles only if the Owner includes them; distinguish each supported embedded host and PTY route.
fixtures.observation_oracle: record the teardown call begin/return, each endpoint's close cause, last complete output sequence and count, process exit evidence and scope emptiness. The consumer cannot be the only observer of the call that can block it. Intentionally retain a duplicated output writer in a negative control. Output closure caused by the harness is labeled local_close, never promoted to all_clients_disconnected.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: reconcile bounded output retention with the selected loss policy and current scope/process state. A drained terminal has no missing acknowledged records; a deliberately truncated terminal has an explicit loss boundary and reason. Either may still have unsettled process work.
fixtures.stop_condition: watchdog-confirmed violation of the chosen bounded teardown contract rejects; lost watchdog or uncertain blocking point yields unknown. Unbounded memory growth while buffering triggers safety stop. Mechanisms: S04, S20, S37.

fixtures.title: Signals and console event scope
fixtures.prerequisites: W, D1 and an unrelated sentinel have distinguishable signal handlers and independent heartbeat evidence. Pin terminal foreground group/session and console sharing.
fixtures.injected_fault: send the chosen graceful cancellation signal/event while D1 ignores it; place D2 in a different process group or console; separately close the terminal transport. Test CTRL_C_EVENT with a nonzero group as an explicit Windows misuse negative control, CTRL_BREAK_EVENT under correct console scope, and Linux foreground/background groups with configured terminal modes.
fixtures.observation_oracle: record API return, handler receipt, continuation heartbeat, native exit and final forced termination as distinct events. The unrelated sentinel must remain unaffected. A successful signal request cannot stand in for recipient acknowledgment or process exit.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: after the graceful deadline, the selected escalation policy targets stable owned identities or scope membership, then verifies emptiness and terminal retention. Any actor beyond the declared signal scope is explicitly accounted for rather than silently treated as signaled.
fixtures.stop_condition: wrong-target delivery or unrelated sentinel death is a safety stop and failed contract. Failure to exit within a promised escalation horizon rejects only when observer completeness is proven; otherwise unknown. Mechanisms: S16, S20, S05.

fixtures.title: Atomic replacement crash cuts
fixtures.prerequisites: preexisting generation A, prepared generation B of different size and digest, observer reads that reopen the authoritative name, and complete same-filesystem/volume route evidence.
fixtures.injected_fault: crash the writer before file flush, after file flush, immediately before replacement, during replacement, after replacement returns, before directory or selected metadata durability step, and after that step before acknowledgment. Include same-directory, cross-directory, cross-filesystem, existing-reader handle, permission-denied and antivirus/filter interference variants where in scope. Windows failure codes with documented partial name states have explicit expected reconciliation branches.
fixtures.observation_oracle: live reopening readers see only states permitted by the selected namespace contract. Preserve native return/error and all relevant names, file IDs, contents, attributes and generations. Readers holding the old file open are interpreted separately from readers reopening the name. No copy-plus-delete fallback may impersonate a successful atomic operation.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: before repairing anything, inventory the original, replacement and backup names and contents, then select or quarantine according to the preregistered algorithm. The witness's acknowledged generation must be recoverable if the selected failure domain promises it. An unacknowledged operation may have completed; recovery must not equate a lost response with no effect.
fixtures.stop_condition: torn/mixed canonical content, a forbidden live namespace gap, or loss of an acknowledged required generation rejects. A documented partial error state handled safely may pass its explicit error contract. Unknown crash ordering remains unknown. Mechanisms: S08, S09, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15.

fixtures.title: Failure domain and power interruption
fixtures.prerequisites: a disposable target; separately powered witness; exact virtual/physical storage/cache topology; approved interruption apparatus; a recoverable test image and written safety procedure.
fixtures.injected_fault: repeat PF06's durability-relevant cuts separately for abrupt process death, guest reset, host reset and actual physical power interruption of the named devices. A graceful shutdown is a control, never the injected crash. For network storage, separately interrupt client power, server power and the declared shared power domain.
fixtures.observation_oracle: E records which power/reset domain actually failed, the last externally witnessed acknowledgment, and evidence that the interruption occurred without a graceful flush path. Device/controller protection and cache behavior are recorded as pins or unknowns. A simulated controller flush failure is a separate synthetic fault, not a physical-power result.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: boot or remount through the frozen recovery procedure, retain the first observed bytes before repair, verify generation and digest, and check application consistency and namespace state. A filesystem checking clean does not establish that the application's acknowledged state survived.
fixtures.stop_condition: any promised acknowledged generation lost or application invariant broken rejects that exact domain. Apparatus uncertainty or inability to inspect the first recovery state yields unknown. An unsafe device, shared production volume or unapproved destructive boundary triggers safety stop. Mechanisms: S11, S14, S30, S33, S34, S35.

fixtures.title: Lock lifetime and mapped bypass
fixtures.prerequisites: two cooperating writers, an independent collision detector, the exact lock primitive/range, and a separate mapped-view actor for the Windows bypass control.
fixtures.injected_fault: terminate the lock owner; close a different descriptor to the same Linux file; retain a duplicate open-file-description reference; request a conflicting lock while release is delayed; and perform mapped-view access while LockFileEx protects the corresponding range. Network variants also interrupt lock ownership/reclamation.
fixtures.observation_oracle: record acquisition completion rather than mere asynchronous submission, the native result/error, competing write attempts, actual overlapping writes and owner identity. A stale lock file's existence is recorded separately from a currently enforced native lock. The mapped bypass control must be detected as outside the primitive's protection.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: a new owner attempts real lock acquisition under a bounded policy, verifies fencing epoch and canonical consistency, and only then resumes. It must not delete a lock marker or assume authority merely because a PID is absent or an elapsed timeout expired. A retained valid reference prevents a premature ownership transfer.
fixtures.stop_condition: two admitted writers or a false exclusivity claim rejects. Release latency beyond a promised bound rejects when proven; no visibility of current server lock ownership yields unknown. Mechanisms: S10, S21, S33.

fixtures.title: PID reuse and stale process identity
fixtures.prerequisites: a disposable process namespace or equivalent safe harness, a stale identity record, a new unrelated sentinel and held original native identity references.
fixtures.injected_fault: let the original process exit and be reaped, then obtain a reuse of its numeric PID through controlled bounded churn or a permitted deterministic namespace facility. Deliver delayed exit, cancellation and recovery messages carrying the stale execution epoch. Also test acquiring pidfd after an unsafe reaping window.
fixtures.observation_oracle: distinguish original process handle/pidfd and creation epoch from numeric PID. The oracle requires proof that reuse actually occurred; exhaustion of the churn budget without reuse is an untriggered cell, not a pass. The negative control uses PID-only targeting and must identify the wrong-target hazard without affecting real processes.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: stale messages cannot affect or settle the new process. Recovery reattaches only when stable identity matches or records unknown and quarantines admission. No broad kill by name or PID enumeration is an acceptable cleanup shortcut.
fixtures.stop_condition: stale cancellation reaches the unrelated sentinel or stale exit settles a new execution: rejected and safety stop. Failure to trigger reuse or resolve identity: unknown. Mechanism: S07; Windows handle preservation is a proposed identity requirement subject to native adapter verification.

fixtures.title: Disk full quota and delayed write failure
fixtures.prerequisites: a disposable bounded filesystem or quota domain that cannot fill the host's system disk, old generation A, independent error logging capacity and a frozen publication sequence.
fixtures.injected_fault: exhaust byte space, inode space or quota independently between content write and flush; inject a short write; surface delayed EIO at flush; deny metadata update during replacement. Windows variants separately capture disk-full, quota and native flush/replacement errors rather than guessing a POSIX mapping.
fixtures.observation_oracle: every write has requested and actual lengths; every flush and rename/replace has its own result. The acknowledgment witness must show no success claimed merely from a completed buffered write. Capture whether error reporting itself failed because its storage was full.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: preserve A or a fully validated B under the selected contract; never accept a truncated B because a name exists. Reconcile pending intent without duplicating externally visible work. Restore space only after recording the failing state and distinguish restored capacity from successful recovery.
fixtures.stop_condition: false durable acknowledgment, torn canonical data or unbounded retry rejects. Loss of independent error evidence produces unknown; spillover to nondisposable storage triggers safety stop. Mechanisms: S31, S11, S08, S09.

fixtures.title: Memory throttling without automatic death inference
fixtures.prerequisites: bounded synthetic allocation workload, a private Linux memory controller domain, baseline hierarchical and local counters, pinned swap/reclaim policy, and controller/witness headroom.
fixtures.injected_fault: drive the workload across memory.high while keeping the hard cap and independent host limits safe; separately impose CPU or I/O throttling to check that the classifier does not confuse stalled progress with memory failure.
fixtures.observation_oracle: correlate native throttle counters, progress cadence, allocation outcomes and live process/scope observations. Report throttle even if the execution later exits normally. A counter delta is interpreted against baseline and hierarchy, not as an event unique to W merely because it was read nearby in time.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: after removing only the test pressure according to the preregistration, determine whether work resumes, remains throttled, fails allocation or requires cancellation. Do not respawn an execution still running under pressure and do not bill throttled wall time as CPU consumption.
fixtures.stop_condition: a portable OOM classification without supporting subtype evidence rejects the classifier. Host pressure escaping the disposable domain is a safety stop. Counter or clock coverage loss yields unknown. Windows has no assumed memory.high equivalent; any substitute is a separately scoped experiment. Mechanisms: S05, S32.

fixtures.title: Memory refusal process kill and group kill
fixtures.prerequisites: safe headroom outside the target scope, native counter snapshots, selected per-process/group limits and explicit OOM group policy. Pin protections/exemptions and external OOM policy agents.
fixtures.injected_fault: hit Linux memory.max under individual and group policies; provoke a bounded allocation refusal path; hit Windows per-process and Job committed-memory limits. A separate harness policy may terminate after a refusal, but its kill must be labeled harness-policy termination rather than native limit behavior.
fixtures.observation_oracle: record allocation API outcomes, native memory events and process identities, which members died, surviving members and whether the controller caused the death. The classifier can emit multiple chronological outcomes, such as throttle then process_kill. It cannot infer group kill from one exit or infer an allocation success from missing notifications.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: account for survivor state and incomplete work before replay; an isolated killed child cannot leave a parent silently committing a partial result. A refusal that was handled successfully does not automatically require replay. Group cleanup and canonical settlement are verified separately.
fixtures.stop_condition: incorrect subtype, unexplained lost members or duplicate retry while survivors run rejects. Global OOM outside the authorized scope is a safety stop. Ambiguous cause of death remains unknown. Mechanisms: S05, S22, S32.

fixtures.title: Supervisor restart and stale owner race
fixtures.prerequisites: isolated test service/unit, frozen restart policy and activation sources, synthetic writer authority epoch and independent supervisor logs.
fixtures.injected_fault: crash B just before and after ownership registration, race automatic restart with manual start/stop, and deliver an old owner's delayed completion after a new owner starts. For Windows include the documented queued SCM restart sequence. For systemd include selected KillMode, timeout and restart policies, plus another activation source if configured.
fixtures.observation_oracle: record every supervisor launch request, execution epoch, stable process identity and admitted writer authority. Service state stopped or active cannot replace native scope evidence. Deliberately retain an old child as a negative control so a new service process cannot make it disappear from accounting.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: exactly one authorized owner may admit work for the intended generation, old epochs remain fenced and all pending restart/activation sources are reconciled. If a restart cannot be prevented under the selected policy, the startup gate must refuse stale work rather than claiming the supervisor is quiescent.
fixtures.stop_condition: dual ownership, stale completion accepted or uncontrolled resurrection rejects. Editing an unrelated service is a safety stop. Missing activation or queued-action visibility produces unknown, not quiescence. Mechanisms: S23, S27, S28.

fixtures.title: Suspend resume and deadline semantics
fixtures.prerequisites: Owner choice between elapsed-time and active-time deadline semantics, identified clocks, external elapsed-time witness, boot epoch and explicit suspend/hibernate/VM pause variants.
fixtures.injected_fault: suspend across a deadline; resume after it; change wall time separately; reboot with a persisted deadline; pause/resume a guest separately from host suspend. Capture each supported sleep state as a distinct variant.
fixtures.observation_oracle: compare pre/post readings and explicit suspend/resume events, accounting for clock resolution and measurement uncertainty. Linux CLOCK_MONOTONIC excludes suspended time while CLOCK_BOOTTIME includes it. Windows unbiased interrupt time excludes sleep/hibernation; other chosen clock behavior must be pinned rather than assumed equivalent. Record the deadline's intended semantics before running. [S19, S17, S18]
fixtures.recovery_oracle: expire once when elapsed semantics require it, or retain the correct remaining active budget when active semantics require it; after reboot reconcile the deadline using the approved epoch policy. A persisted monotonic number from an old boot cannot be treated as a current deadline without conversion evidence.
fixtures.stop_condition: missed or duplicate expiration outside preregistered tolerance rejects; a wrong clock or uncertain pause domain yields unknown. Any action on the real system clock outside the disposable target triggers safety stop.

fixtures.title: Network storage interruption and ambiguous commit
fixtures.prerequisites: isolated client/server test share/export, exact protocol and cache/lease configuration, independent client and server witnesses, no production traffic on the fault path.
fixtures.injected_fault: drop request before server receipt; drop response after server effect; cut connectivity during write, flush, replacement and lock renewal; restart server; recover with both retained and lost server volatile state. Distinguish SMB durable/persistent handle reconnect from ordinary reopen, and NFS verifier/COMMIT and lease recovery variants.
fixtures.observation_oracle: capture request identity, protocol result when available, server evidence, client error and first authoritative post-reconnect state. A timeout is neither not_committed nor committed. A client page-cache read after reconnect is not automatically a server recovery observation.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: verify generation/content against independent acknowledgment; detect changed server identity/verifier or lost locks; reacquire authority through the approved fencing protocol before writes resume. Reissue only when the application's operation identity and semantics make repetition safe. A durable handle is not by itself proof of durable application content.
fixtures.stop_condition: conflicting writers, duplicate nonidempotent publication, false durability claim or forbidden acknowledged data loss rejects. No independent server observation or unconfirmed partition point yields unknown. Mechanisms: S33, S34, S35, S10, S12.

fixtures.title: Lost duplicated and reordered notifications
fixtures.prerequisites: an observation transport where the harness can drop, delay, duplicate and reorder only synthetic notifications, while independent native queries remain available.
fixtures.injected_fault: remove a process exit notification; deliver it twice or after the next execution epoch; overrun an observation buffer; restart the observer while a worker exits; delay Job completion packets and cgroup event reads.
fixtures.observation_oracle: sequence/epoch checks detect duplicates and gaps; authoritative native state resolves what it can; loss of observation coverage is explicit. The negative control removes a notification and must not produce the claim that the event never happened.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: reconcile native identities, canonical record and final accounting. If the event's exact time or cause cannot be reconstructed, retain that unknown even when eventual process death is established. Do not manufacture a timestamp or attribute a counter delta to the wrong execution.
fixtures.stop_condition: silent gap, false success, stale event accepted or unknown converted to zero rejects. Recovery deadline with genuinely insufficient evidence yields unknown. Mechanisms: S01, S05, S07.

fixtures.title: Compatibility path and embedded host boundary
fixtures.prerequisites: a separate instance of every selected MSYS2, Git Bash, WSL and embedded-terminal profile; synthetic filenames and arguments; native child probes with exact expected bytes.
fixtures.injected_fault: launch native children through the compatibility shell; use spaces, Unicode, leading dashes and case collisions in synthetic names; cross a WSL native/Windows mount boundary; terminate the embedded host while retaining the broker. Include environment/path translation and terminal reconnect variants only where the selected adapter uses them.
fixtures.observation_oracle: compare exact arguments, path identities, resulting filesystem route, terminal ownership, process scope and exit evidence. A successful shell command is not proof that the intended native binary or storage route was exercised.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: preserve the same execution identity and canonical data route or reject unsupported reconnect. Host closure must not silently change cancellation, output loss or persistence policy. Qualification belongs to the composite path actually observed.
fixtures.stop_condition: unintended binary/path, accidental profile substitution, lost work hidden by terminal closure or inherited native qualification rejects. Unknown translation or inaccessible host lifecycle remains unknown. Mechanisms: S24, S25, S26, S36, S37.

fixtures.title: Permission and feature denial
fixtures.prerequisites: disposable policy variants with exact security/configuration digests; explicit authorization for every local privilege or policy change.
fixtures.injected_fault: deny Job assignment, cgroup creation/delegation, clone3, pidfd access, lock acquisition, replacement or flush. Provide an unavailable kernel/API feature variant and a present-but-policy-denied variant. No test disables production protections.
fixtures.observation_oracle: native denial code, effective policy and absence or presence of partially created work are recorded. The adapter must not silently fall back to a weaker containment, identity or durability guarantee while preserving the stronger profile label.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: reconcile partial resources, keep admission closed where the promised guarantee is unavailable, and report unsupported for a demonstrably unavailable required feature or unknown for insufficient access to establish capability. The original failing evidence is retained even if a later approved profile change resolves it.
fixtures.stop_condition: undeclared fallback or work released outside the promised policy rejects. Unapproved privilege escalation is a safety stop. Mechanisms: S02, S06, S07, S08, S09.

fixtures.title: Resource accounting completeness
fixtures.prerequisites: W and short lived children have bounded known synthetic workloads, native cumulative counter baselines, stable scope identity and independent observation of child creation/exit.
fixtures.injected_fault: let a child run and exit between sampling intervals, kill the parent first, migrate a process where authorized, lose one counter sample and reset/recreate the scope. Separately retain output after process exit so transport lifetime exceeds compute lifetime.
fixtures.observation_oracle: report counter source, units, aggregation boundary, sampling interval and reset semantics. Distinguish native scope cumulative accounting from samples summed across PIDs. The sum of individual lifetime memory peaks is not a simultaneous group memory peak. Scope membership completeness and descendant capture completeness remain independent tri-state fields.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: return bounded or unknown accounting where a delta cannot be recovered, preserve terminal costs separately from compute, and prevent zero substitution for a missing counter. Reusing a scope name cannot splice two counter epochs into one charge.
fixtures.stop_condition: double count, counter reset read as negative usage, incomplete capture represented as exact or missing value represented as zero rejects. Unavailable native metrics remain unknown and block only claims requiring them. Mechanisms: S01, S05, S22.

fixtures.title: Combined failures and oracle controls
fixtures.prerequisites: all component fixtures have independent evidence and the combined variant list is preregistered. The combined target uses its own exact composite profile.
fixtures.injected_fault: combine output backpressure with supervisor crash; disk-full with writer death; memory pressure with observer restart; network response loss with lock-owner restart; and suspend/resume with cancellation at the deadline. Also run no-fault controls and intentionally faulty adapters for false settlement, omitted flush, PID-only identity and notification-only completion.
fixtures.observation_oracle: each combined fault has its own confirmation and causal order. The intentionally faulty controls must fail the corresponding oracle. A detector that never flags its known-bad control cannot qualify a good-looking run.
fixtures.recovery_oracle: settlement requires all relevant terminal, containment, ownership, accounting and durability predicates, without letting one recovered component mask another unresolved component. Preserve the first failure rather than averaging success and failure repetitions.
fixtures.stop_condition: any violated mandatory invariant rejects; an ineffective fault or insensitive oracle invalidates the cell as unknown. Combined testing does not prove all possible interleavings or substitute for component coverage. Mechanisms: the sources for the component fixtures; the combination design is inferred.
